title: Booking confirmation and welcome
paragraphs: Your call with The Revenue Protocol is booked. I'm Tanmay, one of the co-founders.
Before you leave this page, check that you've received your calendar invitation and add the meeting using the buttons above.

On the call, we'll discuss the retirement clients you want to work with, the states you're licensed in, and how many appointments you can comfortably take each week. From there, we'll look at whether our pay-per-show model makes sense for your business.

We'll walk through how we find and qualify prospects, how appointments reach your calendar, and the pricing for your target asset range. Payment is collected upfront before appointment delivery starts, and we'll explain those terms on the call.

To make that useful, come prepared with three things: your licensed states, the minimum movable assets you want a prospect to have, and your available appointment capacity. If someone else helps approve your marketing spend, invite them too so we can answer their questions together.
Below this video, you'll find our corporate deck and answers to common questions. Reviewing those beforehand gives us more time to discuss your specific situation.

The core of our offer is simple: we handle the advertising, phone screening, booking, and reminders. You pay for qualified appointments that actually take place. No-shows and cancellations are replaced without being billed as held appointments.
If your schedule changes, use the reschedule link so we can find another time.
We're looking forward to learning about your business. See you on the call.

title: What am I paying for?
paragraphs: What am I paying for?

With The Revenue Protocol, you pay for a qualified appointment that actually takes place. That means both you and the prospect attend, and the prospect meets the profile we agreed on during onboarding.
To get that conversation onto your calendar, we handle the advertising, phone screening, booking, and reminders. Your team then takes the meeting and determines whether you can help that person.
Payment is collected upfront before appointment delivery starts. On our call, we'll explain the applicable amount and how the qualification and replacement terms work.

title: Where do the prospects come from?
paragraphs: Where do the prospects come from?
We run Meta and Google ads through our consumer retirement brand, reaching people who are planning for retirement.
When someone responds, they complete a retirement questionnaire. From there, our calling team speaks with them to check whether they fit the requirements you've given us.
That screening happens before we book the appointment with you, so there's a conversation with our team between their initial response to an ad and the meeting on your calendar.

title: How do you qualify each prospect?
paragraphs: How do you qualify each prospect?
We start with the retirement questionnaire, then a US-based caller speaks with the prospect to confirm their age, investable assets, and whether those assets can move.
We use what they tell us in that conversation to check their fit against the profile agreed at onboarding. That's how we determine whether to book them with you.
The asset information is confirmed over the phone with the prospect. You'll still carry out your own fact-finding when you meet them and evaluate their situation.

title: What asset levels can I target?
paragraphs: What asset levels can I target?
Our current minimum is two hundred and fifty thousand dollars in movable assets. If your business focuses on larger cases, you can choose a higher minimum.
Our pricing tiers extend to ten million dollars and above, so we'll discuss which range fits the clients you want to work with.
Bring your preferred minimum to the call. We'll use that to talk through the relevant pricing and delivery expectations for your profile.

title: Can I choose the states where appointments are booked?
paragraphs: Can I choose the states where appointments are booked?
Yes. At onboarding, you tell us which states you're licensed in, along with your target asset range and appointment availability.
We use those requirements to decide which prospects can be booked with you. You'll also provide any disclosure language we need to use as part of that process.
Have your licensed states ready for our call so we can discuss the specific geography you want to serve.

title: Will the prospect know who they're meeting?
paragraphs: Will the prospect know who they're meeting?
Yes. When our caller books the appointment, they introduce you by name and explain the meeting to the prospect.
The prospect also receives preparation material and reminders before the appointment. That gives them context about the conversation and helps them prepare to attend.
When you meet, you can build on that introduction, learn more about their situation, and determine whether your services are a fit.

title: What happens if someone cancels or doesn't show?
paragraphs: What happens if someone cancels or doesn't show?
That appointment is not billed as a held appointment. We return it to our calling team and replace it with another qualified prospect.
The same applies if the prospect cancels. The appointment needs to take place and meet the agreed requirements to count as a qualified, held appointment.
We'll walk through how those replacements and the billing process work on our call so you know what to expect before you start.

title: What if someone attends but doesn't meet the agreed requirements?
paragraphs: What if someone attends but doesn't meet the agreed requirements?

Let us know within forty-eight hours and explain which requirement wasn't met. We review the intake recording against the profile agreed at onboarding, and we credit the appointment if it was unqualified.
If the issue is that the prospect belongs in a different asset tier, we bill the appointment at the correct tier. That adjustment can move the charge up or down.
We'll go through those terms with you before you start, including how to flag an appointment for review.

title: How much does an appointment cost?
paragraphs: How much does an appointment cost?
Pricing depends on the prospect's asset tier. Once we understand the type of client you want to work with, we can walk through the rates that apply to that profile.
Payment is collected upfront before we begin delivering appointments. We'll explain the applicable upfront amount and how the qualification, replacement, and billing terms work before you decide.
That gives you the information to evaluate both the acquisition cost and the cash required to start.

title: Do I pay upfront?
paragraphs: Do I pay upfront?
Yes. Payment is collected upfront before we begin delivering appointments. Pay-per-show defines which qualified, held appointments count for billing.

On our call, we'll explain the rates for your target asset range, the upfront amount, and how qualification and replacement terms work. That way, you can evaluate the arrangement before deciding whether to start.

title: How many appointments can you provide, and when can we start?
paragraphs: How many appointments can you provide, and when can we start?
We'll discuss that based on your licensed states, target asset range, and the number of appointments your calendar can comfortably hold.
Those details let us talk through availability for your specific profile and agree on delivery expectations before you start.
Come to the call with a realistic weekly capacity in mind, including time to follow up after the first appointment. We'll use that as the starting point for the conversation.

title: Do you guarantee that an appointment becomes a client?
paragraphs: Do you guarantee that an appointment becomes a client?
No. Our offer covers qualified appointments that actually take place. Whether someone becomes a client depends on their needs, your recommendations, and your sales process.
That's why we'll discuss your current conversion assumptions when we look at the economics together. If you have results from similar appointments, bring those numbers to the call.
They'll help us evaluate whether the acquisition cost makes sense for your business.

title: Is there a long-term contract?
paragraphs: Is there a long-term contract?
No long-term contract is required, and you can cancel by email.

Before you start, we'll walk through the payment and delivery terms so you understand how the arrangement works, including the process for qualified appointments, replacements, and any billing adjustments.
You can bring any questions about those terms to our call. We want you to understand what you're agreeing to before you make a decision.

title: What should I prepare for the call?
paragraphs: What should I prepare for the call?
Bring three things: the states you're licensed in, the minimum movable assets you want a prospect to have, and how many additional appointments you can take each week.
Those details give us a starting point for discussing the profile and volume that fit your business. If you have your current acquisition costs and conversion estimates handy, bring those as well.
And if someone else helps approve your marketing spend, invite them to join. That way, we can answer everyone's questions in the same conversation.

title: What if I need to change the meeting time?
paragraphs: What if I need to change the meeting time?
If your schedule changes, use the reschedule link in your confirmation email or on this page to choose another available time.
Once you've rescheduled, check the updated invitation and make sure the new time is on your calendar. If someone else from your team is joining, let them know about the change too.
We're looking forward to speaking with you when you have time to focus on the conversation.
